proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: The section e : U to R of s is an immersion (schemes section-immersion lemma). In the displayed diagram, the square with (1, i) on top and e at the bottom is cartesian because a composed with b = e forces b = i(a); the composition of the two horizontal maps is the diagonal morphism of t : R to U, and the right top horizontal arrow is an isomorphism. Since Omega_{R/U} is the conormal sheaf of the composition, it is isomorphic to the conormal sheaf of (1, i); the conormal functoriality lemma for flat base changes then yields the canonical surjection t^*C_{U/R} to Omega_{R/U}, an isomorphism when c is flat; and c is a base change of s by the properties of the pullback diagram (equation-pull), so flatness of s implies flatness of c by the base-change-flat lemma. (source lines 344-370)

core_obligations: The section e : U to R of s is an immersion by schemes-lemma-section-immersion (proof lines 344-347). In the displayed diagram the left square with top arrow (1, i) : R to R times_{s, U, t} R and bottom arrow e : U to R is cartesian, since a composed with b = e forces b = i(a); the composition of the two horizontal maps is the diagonal morphism of t : R to U; the right top horizontal arrow (pr_0, i composed with pr_1) is an isomorphism (proof lines 348-361). Hence Omega_{R/U}, being the conormal sheaf of the composition, is isomorphic to the conormal sheaf of (1, i); by morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial-flat one obtains the canonical surjection t^*C_{U/R} to Omega_{R/U}, an isomorphism if c is flat (proof lines 361-366). Finally c is a base change of s by the properties of diagram (equation-pull), so if s is flat then c is flat by morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat, and the surjection is an isomorphism, proving the flat case (proof lines 366-369).
proof_roadmap: Establish e as an immersion via the section lemma (proof lines 344-347).
Analyze the diagram: cartesian left square, horizontal composition equal to the diagonal of t, right top arrow an isomorphism (proof lines 348-361).
Identify Omega_{R/U} with the conormal sheaf of (1, i) and apply the conormal functoriality lemma for the surjection, with flat c upgrading to an isomorphism (proof lines 361-366).
Transfer flatness from s to c through the pullback diagram and conclude the isomorphism in the flat case (proof lines 366-369).
